subject: sociology
title: Waves and Workplaces
welcome_lead: From the first vote to TikTok activism, ride the three waves of feminism and apply them to today's workplace.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure applying feminism's three waves to workplace inequality and the gender pay gap.
final_note: Pair each wave with a date and a piece of evidence for top marks.

concepts.def: Invisible barrier blocking women from top jobs.
Average difference between men's and women's pay.
Who does paid work and housework at home.

walkthroughs.body_html: First wave won UK women's votes in 1918 (over 30) and 1928 (over 21). Second wave brought the Equal Pay Act 1970 and Sex Discrimination Act 1975. Third wave includes movements like #MeToo from 2017.
The UK gender pay gap (ONS) is around 7-15% depending on the measure. Women are over-represented in caring jobs and under-represented in top boards — the glass ceiling.
Ann Oakley's 1974 study of 40 housewives showed even working women did most housework. Decades later, studies still show women spend more hours per week on unpaid domestic work than men.
